matches_paper_condition: SCRATCH (whole network trained, matching a randomly-initialized backbone; the existing head-only arms match the paper's FINE-TUNING condition, appropriate only for a pretrained backbone)
input_construction: real graph topology with node/edge/angle features resampled from N(0,1), fresh draw every iteration
label_construction: balanced random 0/1 labels, freshly resampled every iteration, unpaired with inputs
budget_principle: identical optimizer-step and batch-size budget to the existing head-only Random2 arms (COORDINATE_NOISE_CONFIG.json's warmup block: optimizer_steps=938, batch_size=128), so the only thing that differs between arms is what is trainable, not how much compute each gets. Not tuned to produce an effect.
batchnorm_running_stats: legitimately update during this warm-up (encoder is invoked every step, unlike the head-only arms) — the existing 'BatchNorm buffers must stay byte-identical' gate does not apply and is replaced by: all parameters/buffers finite after every step; encoder state changed after warm-up (opposite-direction sanity check); full pre/post model-state SHA-256 recorded for provenance.
known_risk: 938 whole-network optimizer steps is a much larger intervention than 938 steps on a 256->2 head alone and may substantially degrade the encoder. If observed, this is reported as a finding (e.g. large parameter drift from init, or degraded downstream accuracy in Stage B), not treated as a reason to shrink this budget after the fact.
